findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "demand.request_introduction" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Ask a specific seller to answer the user about one car from demand.find_vehicle. Call this when the user says they want that one, wants the out-the-door price, …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "demand.list_constraints" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: demand.price_check, demand.introduction_status, demand.create_watch · Private data: demand.create_watch, demand.list_watches, demand.cancel_watch · Public sink: demand.search, demand.request_introduction, demand.introduction_status, demand.capabilities, demand.create_watch, demand.list_watches, demand.ask.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: demand.price_check, demand.introduction_status, demand.create_watch · Private data: demand.create_watch, demand.list_watches, demand.cancel_watch · Public sink: demand.search, demand.request_introduction, demand.introduction_status, demand.capabilities, demand.create_watch, demand.list_watches, demand.ask

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
